name: MC7912BTG
title: MC7900 series 1.0 A fixed negative voltage regulators
summary: Three-terminal linear regulators with fixed negative outputs of -5.0, -5.2, -6.0, -8.0, -12, -15, -18 and -24 V, the negative counterparts of the MC7800 series. They limit their own current, shut down when too hot and cut back their short-circuit limit as input-output voltage rises, and deliver more than 1.0 A when heatsunk. A grades hold 2% output tolerance; B and C grades 4%. TO-220 and D2PAK packages, tab tied to the input.
key_figures: -35 V max (-5 to -18 V parts), -40 V (24 V part)

notes: T suffix: TO-220; D2T suffix: D2PAK; G suffix: Pb-free lead finish.

circuits.title: Standard application
circuits.description: The regulator alone between a negative input and its fixed negative output, with a 0.33 µF capacitor across the input and a 1.0 µF capacitor across the output, both returned to the ground shared by input and output. Cin is needed when the regulator sits far from the supply's filter capacitor; CO improves stability and transient response.
notes: XX is the nominal output voltage in the type number.
The input must stay typically 2.0 V more negative than the output, including at the high point of the input ripple.

circuits.title: Current regulator
circuits.description: An MC7905 from a -20 V input drives a 10 Ω resistor from OUT to its own GND pin, so it holds 5.0 V across the resistor and sinks a constant 200 mA through the load connected at the GND pin node. The load current is the resistor current plus the regulator's bias current; the load may take up to 10 V. 1.0 µF capacitors sit across the input and the output to ground, positive sides on ground.

circuits.title: Current boost regulator, -5.0 V at 4.0 A with 5.0 A current limiting
circuits.description: An external 2N3055 carries most of the load current from the -10 V input to the -5.0 V output, its base driven from the regulator's input node, which is fed from the input through 5.6 Ω. Three 0.56 Ω resistors in parallel sense the pass current in the 2N3055's emitter; when their drop turns on the MJE200, it pulls the regulator's input node toward the input and limits the pass transistor. The short-circuit current is the sum of the pass-stage and regulator limits, 3.2 A and 1.8 A in this circuit; the pass-stage limit is about 0.6 V/RSC. The regulator and both transistors are on a heatsink.
notes: Driving past the 5.0 A point toward the regulator's own peak current needs the regulator on a heatsink; otherwise it shuts down thermally when it takes up the extra current.

circuits.title: Operational amplifier supply
circuits.description: An MC7815 and an MC7915 make ±15 V from ±20 V for operational amplifiers. Each regulator has 1.0 µF from input and from output to ground, with a further 0.33 µF on the positive input. A 1N4001G runs between each regulator's output and input, and another from each output to ground; the clamp on the MC7815 output prevents latch-up when the positive output is pulled below ground with more than 200 mA.

circuits.title: Protection diodes
circuits.description: An MC7915 from -20 V to -15 V with 1.0 µF on input and output and two Schottky diodes. D1, from output to ground, stops the output being driven to the opposite polarity during start-up, power-down and short circuit. D2, from input to output, gives the output capacitor a path that bypasses the regulator if the input is shorted or the supply switches off fast.
notes: Below 10 µF of output capacitance a protection diode is generally not needed.

equations.name: Current regulator output current
equations.note: The -5.0 V part is used so dissipation stays low and the output can come within 6.0 V of the input.

where.ILIM: current at which the series pass stage limits
where.RSC: sense resistance in the pass transistor's emitter

operation.text: Three protections are built in: thermal overload shuts the regulator down under excessive dissipation; short-circuit limiting caps the current it passes; and safe-area compensation lowers the short-circuit current as the input-output voltage rises.

Many low-current uses run without capacitors. Bypass the input when the regulator is on long leads from the supply filter or the load capacitance is large: 0.33 µF or more, tantalum, mylar or another type with low impedance at high frequency and ESR under 0.7 Ω, with the shortest leads straight across the input terminals. Bypassing the output is recommended as well.
There is no remote sense pin, so ground loops and voltage drops in the leads appear in the output; keep the wiring short and the ground common to input and output.
The input must stay typically 2.0 V more negative than the output, even at the top of the input ripple.

External capacitors can discharge into low-current points of the regulator, or the output can be forced to the opposite polarity. Below 10 µF of output capacitance no diode is usually needed. A diode from output to ground guards against polarity reversal at start-up, power-down and short circuit; a diode from input to output lets the output capacitor discharge around the regulator when the input is shorted or switched off quickly.
Paired with an MC7815 the part forms a ±15 V supply. A clamp diode at the MC7815 output stops latch-up if the positive output is pulled below ground with more than 200 mA.

Line regulation: output change for an input change, measured at low dissipation or with pulses so the die temperature barely moves. Load regulation: output change for a load change at fixed die temperature. Maximum power dissipation: the total device dissipation up to which the specifications hold. Input bias current: the share of input current not delivered to the load. Output noise voltage: rms output AC over a stated band, with constant load and no input ripple. Long-term stability: output drift in accelerated life test at maximum rated voltage and maximum dissipation.

TO-220 parts read MC over 79xxACT, 7905.2CT, 79xxBT or 79xxCT; D2PAK parts read MC over 79xxACD2T, 79xxBD2T or 79xxCD2T; xx is the nominal voltage. The third line is AWLYWWG: assembly location, wafer lot, year, work week, and G for Pb-free.
